skill.name: xcrawl-crawl
skill.description: Use this skill for XCrawl crawl tasks, including bulk site crawling, crawler rule design, async status polling, and delivery of crawl output for downstream scrape and search workflows.
skill.summary: Create bounded XCrawl jobs, configure extraction options, and retrieve asynchronous crawl results.
skill.author: xcrawl-api

security_audit.summary: All 132 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, documented configuration, or legitimate XCrawl authentication and API calls. A separate finding concerns the documented default that disables target TLS verification; both usage examples omit a secure override. No evidence found of malicious credential exfiltration, destructive operations, or embedded prompt injection.

remediation.issue: Target TLS verification is documented as disabled by default, and neither usage example overrides this setting.
remediation.suggestion: Explicitly set request.skip_tls_verification to false in both examples and workflow guidance. Require informed approval before disabling certificate checks.

semantic_findings.title: Documented TLS Verification Bypass Default
semantic_findings.description: The request table lists skip_tls_verification with default true. Both examples omit an override, potentially allowing intercepted or tampered target responses when following the documented default.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The insecure default and omitted overrides are explicit in the source. Confidence concerns the documented workflow; actual upstream enforcement was not tested.

content.user_title: Crawl Websites with Bounded XCrawl Jobs
content.value_statement: Bulk website collection requires clear crawl boundaries and asynchronous result tracking. This skill guides XCrawl requests, filtering rules, and retrieval of original API responses.
actual_capabilities: Create XCrawl jobs and retrieve results through the documented create and result endpoints.
Configure page limits, crawl depth, URL filters, domain boundaries, and sitemap use.
Set proxy location, request locale, device type, cookies, headers, and browser rendering options.
Request HTML, Markdown, links, summaries, screenshots, or structured extraction with a prompt and schema.
Configure webhook URLs, headers, and lifecycle events for asynchronous callbacks.
Track job states and return request details, original responses, and upstream errors.
limitations: Requires an XCrawl account, available credits, and an API key stored in a local configuration file.
Depends on network access, curl or Node, and the external XCrawl service.
Provides instructions and examples, not a bundled crawler implementation or guaranteed website coverage.
Returns original responses by default; derived summaries require an explicit request.

use_cases.title: Collect Documentation for Search
use_cases.description: Crawl an approved documentation section with path filters and page limits, requesting Markdown and links for later indexing.

use_cases.title: Extract Public Research Data
use_cases.description: Configure structured extraction for authorized public pages and retrieve the completed job responses for later analysis.

use_cases.title: Inspect Rendered Site Content
use_cases.description: Request rendered pages and screenshots for a bounded website section, using desktop or mobile viewport settings.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Crawl
prompt_templates.prompt: Crawl [approved site URL] with a 10-page limit and depth 1. Request Markdown, keep TLS verification enabled, and return the original responses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: collect a small, bounded sample.

prompt_templates.title: Collect a Documentation Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Crawl [approved documentation URL], including only /docs/ paths and excluding /blog/. Limit to 100 pages and depth 2. Request Markdown and links. Keep TLS verification enabled and return original create and result responses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: apply inclusion and exclusion rules.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Structured Page Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Crawl [approved site URL] with a 50-page limit and depth 2. Extract [fields] using [schema] and request links. Use [locale] and [device]. Keep TLS verification enabled. Poll until completion or failure and return original responses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine structured extraction with request settings.

prompt_templates.title: Configure an Asynchronous Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a crawl for [approved site URL] with [page limit], [depth], and [path filters]. Configure [approved HTTPS webhook] for completed and failed events. Keep external links excluded and TLS verification enabled. Confirm scope before starting. Return original API responses.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate crawl boundaries and callback delivery.

output_examples.input: Describe an illustrative request for a documentation crawl limited to 20 pages and depth 2.
output: Illustrative request: documentation paths only, 20-page limit, depth 2, Markdown and links, with TLS verification enabled.
The create response supplies a task identifier and an initial pending status.
The result response reports job status, available page data, and credit usage.

output_examples.input: Describe the expected response delivery when an approved crawl fails. Do not invent live results.
output: The endpoint flow and submitted request payload accompany the original create and result response bodies.
Any upstream error details are returned without presenting speculative page counts as completed coverage.
No derived summary is added unless explicitly requested.

best_practices: Set explicit page limits, depth, and path filters before starting any crawl.
Keep TLS verification enabled and restrict crawl targets and webhook destinations to approved locations.
Protect the local API key file and avoid sharing secrets in request payloads, logs, or conversation output.
anti_patterns: Starting broad crawls without explicit scope, page limits, or authorization.
Accepting the documented TLS verification bypass default for ordinary production targets.
Treating an initial pending status or estimated page count as proof of completed coverage.

faq.question: What must I configure before using this skill?
faq.answer: Create ~/.xcrawl/config.json with your XCRAWL_API_KEY. An XCrawl account, available credits, network access, and curl or Node are required.

faq.question: Does the skill run a local crawler?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for calling the external XCrawl service through curl or Node.

faq.question: How can I restrict crawl scope?
faq.answer: Set page limits, maximum depth, and include or exclude filters. Keep subdomains and external links excluded unless explicitly needed.

faq.question: Which output formats are documented?
faq.answer: HTML, raw HTML, Markdown, links, summaries, screenshots, and JSON are documented. Structured extraction supports a prompt and schema.

faq.question: How are asynchronous results retrieved?
faq.answer: Start a crawl, record its identifier, and poll the result endpoint until completed or failed. Webhook configuration is also documented.

faq.question: What security setting needs attention?
faq.answer: The guide documents skip_tls_verification as true by default. Set it to false to retain target certificate verification.
